0.0.n: This noun specifies what the anniversary celebrates.

0.1.n: 周年 counts years since something began, marking an anniversary.

0.2.n: Placed after an anniversary, this noun announces a celebration of that milestone.

0.4.n: This describes titles spanning the movie series’ history, rather than just recent ones.

0.5.n: This borrowed word refers to Blu-ray editions of the films.

0.6.n: が marks the Blu-rays as the subject of the release announcement.

0.7.n: This noun refers to making a product available to buy.

0.8.n: だ is a casual statement ending used after nouns, here announcing the release.

0.9.n: ゾ is an emphatic sentence ending; katakana gives it a playful, distinctive look.

1.0.n: 懐かしい expresses fond feelings about the past; です makes the statement polite.

1.1.n: なぁ adds a lingering, reflective feeling, as if the speaker is savoring a memory.

2.0.n: この comes directly before a noun, here pointing to the period being shown.

2.1.n: 頃 refers to an approximate period rather than an exact moment.

2.2.n: の links the time period to オラ, identifying the speaker’s younger self.

2.3.n: オラ is a rustic, informal way to refer to oneself, used here as the character’s distinctive speech.

2.5.n: ちょっと softens the description, making it sound less strong.

2.6.n: 幼い becomes 幼くない in the negative; rising question intonation invites agreement that the speaker looks young.

3.0.n: This duration tells us how long the release schedule will take.

3.1.n: The て-form of かける follows a duration to express spending that amount of time on something.

3.2.n: 発売する becomes 発売して, then adds いく to describe releases continuing forward from now.

3.3.n: ゾ adds confident emphasis to the announcement, with a playful katakana spelling.

0.lit: Movies’ 30th-anniversary commemoration! Blu-rays from throughout the years are being released, I tell you!
0.tip: 発売だ is a compact, casual way to announce a product release.

1.tip: なぁ makes the polite statement sound reflective and warmly emotional.

2.lit: The me of this time, don't I look a little young?
2.tip: A negative question like 幼くない？ often seeks agreement: the speaker thinks they do look young.

3.lit: Taking one year, they will go on releasing them, I tell you!
3.tip: 発売していく describes releases progressing over time, not all happening at once.
